domains.title: The Careful One
domains.subtitle: Goddess of Oaths and Knowledge
domains.lead: Vǫr is one of the Ásynjur, the goddesses who attend Frigg in Ásgarðr. Her name means "the careful one" or "the aware one," and Snorri says that nothing can be hidden from her. She is the goddess who sees through deception, remembers oaths, and knows the truth that others try to conceal.

cards.name: Nothing Hidden
cards.desc: Snorri says Vǫr is so wise that nothing can be concealed from her — the divine witness to every secret.

cards.name: Oath-Keeper
cards.desc: She oversees sworn agreements and remembers the words spoken in haste or hope.

cards.name: Wise Counselor
cards.desc: Among Frigg's attendants she is the one whose knowledge makes her counsel valuable.

cards.name: Vǫr's Watchfulness
cards.desc: Her care is not anxiety but attention: the steady gaze that knows what is real.

symbols.name: Scales or balance
symbols.meaning: The weighing of oaths and the justice of remembered words

symbols.name: Mirror
symbols.meaning: Reflection and self-knowledge; she shows things as they are

symbols.name: The open book
symbols.meaning: The record of oaths, laws, and hidden truths

mythology.lead: Vǫr's mythology is limited to Snorri's catalogue of the Ásynjur, but her function is clear and important.

myths.title: The All-Seeing Goddess
myths.text: In Snorri's list of goddesses, Vǫr is described as wise and inquiring: "She is wise and enquiring, so that nothing can be concealed from her." Her name is given as the source of the adjective vǫrr, "careful, aware." The brief entry makes her a personification of attentiveness — the quality that turns mere seeing into knowledge.

myths.title: Among the Wise Goddesses
myths.text: Vǫr appears alongside Sága, Eir, Gefjun, and Fulla as one of Frigg's attendants. Unlike some Ásynjur who have individual myths, Vǫr is defined entirely by her attribute: she is the one who knows. In a pantheon where Óðinn seeks wisdom through sacrifice and deception, Vǫr represents a quieter, more constant form of knowledge.

myths.title: The Careful Name
myths.text: The name Vǫr is related to Old Norse words for being, awareness, and carefulness. It is not a common noun like Þrúðr ("strength") but an adjective made divine. She is carefulness personified — the virtue that notices before it judges and remembers before it forgives.

lore.syncretism: Vǫr has no clear foreign equivalent, but her function — the all-seeing goddess of oaths and truth — overlaps with several figures. The Greek Themis and Roman Fides both watch over sworn agreements; the Egyptian Maat personifies truth and cosmic order. Within Norse tradition she is close to Sága, who also knows hidden things, and to Frigg herself, whose knowledge is said to rival Óðinn's. The comparison is functional, not historical: Vǫr is the minor goddess who makes the major virtue visible.
lore.culturalLegacy: Vǫr is rarely a central figure in modern retellings, but her name and attribute persist in discussions of Norse goddess-lore. She is sometimes invoked in Heathen practice for matters of truth-telling, oath-keeping, and discernment. The restoration Vǫr preserves the long ǫ that distinguishes the Old Norse careful one from the modern English homophone. Her legacy is the reminder that knowledge begins with attention.
lore.extendedMeditation:
Vǫr is the goddess who pays attention. In a world of masks and boasts, she is the one who notices the small contradiction, the slipped word, the glance that does not match the smile. Her wisdom is not the wisdom of the runes or the mead of poetry; it is the older wisdom of simply seeing what is there.

To invoke Vǫr is to invoke honesty — first with oneself. She is the witness who cannot be deceived because she does not deceive herself. In an age of misinformation, she is the goddess we most need and most neglect.

lore.archaeology: Vǫr is a purely textual figure. No runestone, image, or place-name is securely hers. Her only witnesses are the manuscripts of Snorri's Prose Edda and the associated þulur.
